articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702's warrantless surveillance finally hit its expiration date, proving that even the surveillance state occasionally loses track of time. A rare victory for those who prefer their communications unmonitored by alphabet soup agencies.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor decided to make AWS GovCloud keys public on GitHub because apparently cybersecurity agencies need to practice what they preach the hard way. Congress is now demanding answers while we all slowly clap.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters exploited an Oracle zero-day to absolutely ransack higher education networks. Nothing says 'disrupting academia' like stealing student data through unpatched enterprise software.

articles.title: The new BitLocker exploit everyone's freaking out about probably won't affect you
articles.summary: Chinese hackers backdoored Linux PAM and OpenSSH for nearly a decade, turning login systems into their personal red carpet. This is why we can't have nice things or trust our authentication stack.

articles.title: Privacy own-goal: World Cup blunder leaks Lionel Messi’s passport details
articles.summary: Nightmare Eclipse continues their personal vendetta against Microsoft with RoguePlanet and GreatXML privilege escalation exploits. When bug hunting becomes performance art with actual bite.

articles.title: U.S. Orders Anthropic to Suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Access for Foreign Nationals
articles.summary: Splunk Enterprise served up a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated remote code execution because apparently even security platforms need security. CVE-2026-20253 scores a perfect 9.8 for maximum chaos potential.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch User Repository packages got hijacked to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits. The supply chain attack that makes you question whether rolling your own packages was ever a good idea.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers tricked Meta's AI support bot into resetting Instagram accounts, briefly turning Obama's White House page into Iranian propaganda. When artificial intelligence meets social engineering, chaos ensues.

articles.title: Oracle warns of security bug that hackers abused to breach 100+ companies | TechCrunch
articles.summary: $46.75M settlement for 23andMe's 2023 data breach proves that your genetic privacy has a specific dollar value. At least victims get compensated while their DNA blueprints float around the dark web.

articles.title: Lawmakers Demand Answers as CISA Tries to Contain Data Leak
articles.summary: Netherlands seized 800 servers and arrested hosting providers helping Russia wage cyber warfare across the EU. Sometimes the good guys actually win one and shut down the digital artillery.
